# Claude Code Tray

> A native Windows (10/11) system-tray monitor for Claude Code usage. It shows your
> rate-limit usage percentage as a crisp, DPI-aware vector icon, projects when you'll
> hit 100% (a pace line for the weekly window, burn-rate regression for the 5h session),
> and provides a privacy-first 24h usage breakdown computed locally. Built in C# (.NET 10,
> WinForms + GDI+). Zero configuration — it reuses the OAuth token Claude Code already
> stores on your machine. Installable via the Windows Package Manager:
> `winget install alegauss.ClaudeCodeTray`.

This is an unofficial, open-source community project (Apache License 2.0). It is not
affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are
trademarks of Anthropic; the tool only reads usage data Claude Code already exposes locally.

## Features

- **Crisp at any DPI**: the percentage is drawn as a vector at the exact tray size (no downscaled bitmaps), sharp on 125–200% displays.
- **Task-Manager-style fill bar**: a vertical bar rises with usage; blue when on track, vivid red when projected to exhaust before the window resets.
- **Smart projection**: warns before the window resets, not after. The weekly (7d) window uses a proportional pace line (usage vs. the share an even burn would have spent by now), accurate from the first reading; the 5h session and extra windows use least-squares regression over a short rolling history of utilization samples.
- **Activity-aware weekly pacing**: the Statistics window's weekly projection is spent along the hours you are actually active — a 168-bucket day-of-week x hour profile mined from the timestamps in your local transcripts — instead of uniformly across the clock. It stays flat through the stretches you are usually idle (shaded faintly on the chart) and climbs through your working hours, so the exhaustion marker lands at a plausible time rather than at 4 a.m. Needs about three weeks of local transcripts; below that it falls back to the straight average-pace line. The even-pace line, the verdict chip and the tray icon stay wall-clock. When it projects running out early it also names the earliest hour you normally work that you could resume at and still finish the week under the limit ("stop now and pick it back up around Thursday 13:00, and you'd close the week at about 97%"), or says nothing if no such hour exists. Last week's burn-up is drawn faintly behind the current one on the same axes once two weeks of history exist, answering "is this week worse than the last?" without a second chart or a new number. CLI: `--activity` prints the measured week as a heatmap.
- **Live throughput**: under each Statistics chart, a second number on a second clock. The window average answers "what did this window cost"; below it, "Now ~ N tok/s" answers "what is running now". The moving picture behind that number has its own third tab, **Throughput**: two line charts of the last three minutes - one line per project above, one per token type below, both always drawn - with both window averages beneath them for scale. It lives on its own tab because it is the only thing in the window with no window scope, so "now" was otherwise the same picture on both pace tabs. Read from the local transcripts as they are appended - a byte-level tail with a filesystem watcher, no extra API calls and no change to the rate-limit polling cadence. What the lines plot is the rolling rate (the same age-weighted 60s kernel as the number above them, sampled once a second, attack-smoothed the same way), not the raw per-second counts: a turn's tokens are recorded in the second it finished, so the raw buckets are events, and joining events with a line would draw a rate that never existed. A rolling rate is continuous - it slides down through a pause because the work really is ageing out of the window and climbs when new work lands - and its right-hand end equals the number printed above. Neither chart is a mode: an earlier single chart switched from the by-type view to the by-project view when a second repo started generating, which changed what its colours meant mid-read. Each project keeps a fixed colour and legend position for as long as it has anything on screen, and a repo that goes quiet decays toward zero and ages off the left edge instead of vanishing. Height is a quantity: each chart's ceiling is ruled and labelled in tok/s at the right edge with its half on a dashed line, taken from the highest point visible rounded up to a readable step - or, when the peak is more than 2x the 95th percentile of the moving samples, the percentile instead, with the runs above it drawn dashed along the ceiling rather than silently truncated. Hover states what full height means, how many samples ran past it and what the real peak was; the axis is dropped while a chart is flat. Both numbers are token throughput, not quota, and an empty chart means no turn landed on this machine (work on another machine or on claude.ai leaves no transcript here). The row also reports how many sessions are active (a session counts as active on a turn in the last two minutes, not on file presence); the heaviest four repos get a line and the rest fold into one grey "others". CLI: `--live` prints the rate, the active-session count, the per-project split with each project's slot and every series as a sparkline; `--tail` prints turns as they land.
- **Color-coded reset notifications**: when a usage window hands quota back, a bespoke on-brand toast (confetti + a refilling quota bar) appears, with a distinct color/headline per kind — clay "Surprise!" (early weekly reset), violet "Bonus!" (mid-window credit), teal "New week!" (routine weekly reset), blue "Fresh session!" (5h session reset). All on by default; each toggles independently in Settings.
- **24h usage insights**: local, cost-weighted breakdown by model, subagents, and large-context requests — read only from session transcripts, never message content.
- **Context load inspector**: shows what every session in a project loads *before the first prompt* — the instruction chain, the memory index and every skill/agent description — as a session-zero gauge against the 200k window, with Claude Code's own ~32k system-prompt overhead as its own segment and the transcript-measured startup context overlaid. Splits eager (paid every request) from lazy (paid only when used), annotates each skill "45x" or "never" from real invocations, grades each project A-F, tracks weekly drift, and reports grounded findings (oversized memory index, dead index pointers, memory directories duplicated between worktrees, dead project directories, oversized skill descriptions) each with a concrete fix. Read-only: the single action is copying a cleanup prompt for Claude Code. CLI: `--context`, `--context --check`, `--context --usage`, `--context-report <file.md>`.
- **System information page**: a read-only Settings page that answers "which plan is this login on, and what is this install?" without opening a JSON file. Names the plan the way a person says it (the `userRateLimitTier` behind it mapped to e.g. "Claude Max 5x", with the raw tier, seat tier and billing type as its qualifier, and an unrecognized tier shown verbatim rather than hidden), plus whether extra usage is enabled, when this login first spent a token through Claude Code, and how long the stored sign-in is valid. Then the install: CLI version (the newest in the native installer's version store), install method, auto-update state, how many projects Claude Code tracks, and the configuration folder with a button to open it (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` honoured). Then the machine: the tray's version and location, the Windows build, the .NET runtime and the architecture. The account holder, the email and every absolute path are **masked by default** (initials, `a•••••@example.com`, paths folded back to `~`) because this is the page that ends up in a screenshot attached to a bug report; one button reveals them and hides them again, and "Copy for a bug report" copies the page as plain text exactly as displayed, so a masked holder stays masked. Every reading comes from files Claude Code already keeps locally (`.claude.json`, `.claude/.credentials.json`) — no API call, nothing written, no transcript read, and no secret displayed: the credentials file is read only for its expiry, subscription type and the number of granted permissions.
- **Several Claude Code profiles on one machine**: Claude Code stores one account per configuration directory (`.claude.json` holds a single `oauthAccount`, `/login` overwrites it), so several subscriptions on one Windows means several config dirs via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. The tray discovers every one of them — the dir it would itself use, `~/.claude`, an `env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in either one's `settings.json`, the same key in each registered project's `.claude/settings.json`/`settings.local.json`, and the `~/.claude-*` naming convention — and the System information page offers a picker that re-reads the whole page from the chosen profile's own files. Identity is the account uuid, so the same account reached through two paths is listed once; labels are derived (organization name, else "Personal", else the folder name) and never typed. With a single profile, which is the normal case, the picker is hidden entirely. Read-only: discovery opens files and never writes one. CLI: `--profiles [dir...]`.
- **Auth recovery**: on an expired token (HTTP 401) the tooltip shows a clear "not authenticated" prompt and an "Open Claude Code" menu item re-authenticates in one click.
- **Self-updating**: checks GitHub Releases and offers a one-click in-app update; per-user install, no admin rights.

## Installation

- **winget (recommended)**: `winget install alegauss.ClaudeCodeTray` — published to the Microsoft winget-pkgs community repository, with `en-US` and `pt-BR` manifest locales.
- **Direct download**: run `ClaudeTray-Setup.exe` from the latest GitHub release. Per-user install (no admin); existing installs self-update from GitHub Releases.
- **Prerequisite**: Claude Code installed and logged in at least once (`claude`), so the OAuth token exists at `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`.

## Data source

- Rate-limit data: one minimal Anthropic API call (Haiku, 1 token) every 5 minutes reads the `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` response headers, using the OAuth token at `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`.
- Usage insights: read locally from Claude Code session transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` — no API call.
